correctness.rationale: The 5-tap kernel is rederived from five-point quadratic least squares, and preserves constants. Layer-cake/coarea reduces the unrestricted real-input seminorm to all binary cuts. A standalone exact-integer exhaustive checker verified all 472 nontrivial cuts at n=5,6,7,8 and the displayed sharp maxima \(L_5=6/7\), \(L_6=101/105\), \(L_7=69/70\), \(L_8=251/245\), including consecutive-arc witnesses. An exact 5-nonzero/zero pair count proves the impulse formula for every n>=5, giving strict amplification for every n>=8. A cyclic-shift triangle inequality proves the universal 47/35 upper bound; impulse ratios approach it. No finite experiments are extrapolated to infinite dimensions; unproved exact coefficients n>=9 explicitly withheld.

The original 1964 paper, the 2011 frequency-domain treatment, and the 2014 full technical derivation were compared by mathematical claim; the public index hits concern positivity defect and different finite-difference minimax functionals. value.rationale: This canonical quadratic local-polynomial smoother has negative end weights, so reduction in least-squares noise is not a guarantee of reduction in total pairwise dispersion. Its sharp n=8 loss-of-nonexpansivity boundary, exact base norms, and sharp 47/35 all-ring amplification envelope give a natural dimension-complete stability classification; it is not a renaming of the known coefficient table or an arbitrary narrow parameter slice. Sources: Savitzky-Golay 1964, Schafer 2011, Candan-Inan 2014; the indexed filter positivity-defect paper is a related but distinct endpoint result.
